# Cashing out long service leave

After an employee has fully accrued a long service leave entitlement, an employer and employee can agree to the employee receiving a cash benefit instead of the leave.

Last updated: 13 May 2026

A long service leave entitlement cannot be ‘cashed out’ in advance

It is not permitted for a long service leave entitlement to be ‘cashed out’ in advance of the employee having completed the necessary [continuous employment](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/what-continuous-employment "What is continuous employment?") (that is prior to the leave being accrued), either:

- through a lump sum payment;
- incrementally through an extra amount paid on top of a base rate of pay; or
- through a commission payment.

Under the [WA _Long Service Leave Act_,](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/coverage-of-the-long-service-leave-act "Coverage of the Long Service Leave Act") an employer and employee are able to agree to cash out some or all of an employee's long service leave **only once** the employee has completed the necessary period of [continuous employment](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/what-continuous-employment "What is continuous employment?") and fully accrued the entitlement (after 10 years of continuous employment and then after each subsequent 5 years of continuous employment).

When an employee cashes out long service leave, they must be paid at least the amount of ordinary pay they would have received had they taken the leave. This is to ensure that an employee who cashes out accrued long service leave is not financially worse off for cashing out their leave than taking the leave.

**An agreement to cash out long service leave must be in writing and signed by the employer and employee.**

The employer must keep a copy of the written agreement, including details of the amount of leave and the dollar value of the long service leave cashed out.

An employee who cashes out their long service leave rather than taking the leave **does not accrue** annual leave, personal leave or long service leave on the leave that is cashed out.

_Example_

> _Emma has worked for Ryan for 11_ _years, and has accrued a long service leave entitlement for 8.667_ _weeks after 10_ _years’ continuous employment._
>
> _Emma requests to cash out 4_ _weeks of the 8.667_ _weeks’ leave she has accrued. Ryan agrees to this, and he prepares a written agreement for them both to sign, specifying that Emma will receive an amount equivalent to 4_ _weeks’ salary as payment for the cashed out long service leave._

For information on entitlements under this scheme, contact [MyLeave](http://www.myleave.wa.gov.au/)

Require translating and interpreting assistance when calling Wageline? Use the [Translating and Interpreting Service](https://www.tisnational.gov.au/) on 13 14 50.

[National Relay Service](https://www.accesshub.gov.au/) helps people who are deaf, hearing and/or speech-impaired contact Wageline. Call the National Relay Service on 13 36 77 and ask to call Wageline on 1300 655 266.
